clue.text: Scene from the past of vulgar rugby player

parts.note: flash means showy in a cheap, vulgar way
a back is a rugby position behind the forwards

explanation.surface: A memory of some crude rugby player from years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar rugby player' reads as one person, but the adjective and the position are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In films and novels, a flashback is an interrupting episode set earlier in the story's timeline.

clue.text: Song of fire and ice, both essentially over

parts.note: a flame is fire

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so from each of two words only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of this three-letter word
the central letter of this three-letter word
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A ballad about fire and ice, with both of them finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both essentially' applies to 'and' as well as 'ice', which is easy to miss because 'and' looks like a mere joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is an Andalusian musical tradition that includes passionate Spanish gypsy singing, as well as dance and guitar.

clue.text: A cereal heard to surprise

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what is heard is judged only by its sound, so a word spelt differently but said the same will do

parts.note: maize is a cereal crop, also called corn

explanation.surface: A breakfast food that apparently is meant to astonish.
explanation.walkthrough: The grain MAIZE and the puzzle MAZE are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to astonish someone or catch them unawares with something unexpected.

clue.text: Sanctimonious husband's lie on oath hurt badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pious husband is badly wounded by the lie he told under oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurt' looks like the verb of the sentence but is part of the letters to be rearranged; the indicator is 'badly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sanctimonious acts morally superior to others, which is what this hyphenated idiom describes.

clue.text: Pilot found in area by hill

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
via means by way of
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A pilot is located in a region next to a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a position word joining area and hill, but it supplies three letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is someone who flies aircraft, an old-fashioned synonym for an airline or military pilot.

clue.text: King and queen stifle sign of hesitation about hollowed out fruit

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother or muffle, so one pair of letters closes around another

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
um is what people say while hesitating
QU is an abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: a thing hollowed out has lost its insides, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: only the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A royal couple suppress their hesitation over some fruit with its insides scooped out.
explanation.walkthrough: The king and queen letters close around the hesitation, and the ends of 'about' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The kumquat is a small orange citrus fruit eaten whole, peel and all.

clue.text: Ruler requests a refund in part

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the phrase, sitting inside the run of letters

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole article and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A monarch asks for some of his money back.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across three words: requesTS A Refund.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917, an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Material from extortionist's family

parts.note: a loan shark or swindler is called a shark; with the possessive 's
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Cloth obtained from a racketeer's relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive is kept as a letter: the shark's kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharkskin is a smooth worsted or rayon fabric with a slightly lustrous, textured finish, used for suits.

clue.text: Stay on team

parts.note: re means on, as in concerning
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Remain part of the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: RE in the sense 'on the subject of' is a staple crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or dwell somewhere, so staying in a place is a close synonym.

clue.text: Drab debutante dancing first part of rumba routine

indicators.note: dancers move about and change places, so the letters do too

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dull young society girl doing the opening steps of a Latin dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' and 'rumba' both belong to the ballroom picture, but one shuffles letters and the other donates its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the phrase means basic, everyday and dependable, the ordinary routine work that pays the bills.

clue.text: Be of service to one stuck in revolting volcanic discharge

indicators.note: to revolt is literally to turn round, so the letters run backwards
something stuck in another thing sits inside it

parts.note: lava is molten rock thrown out by a volcano
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Help someone trapped in disgusting molten rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' poses as 'disgusting', but here it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail someone is to help or benefit them, an old-fashioned way of saying be useful.

clue.text: Moralist upset about male gods

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters go round another
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A preacher of morals is offended by male deities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as 'offended' but signals rearranging; the rearranged letters then go round the male abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The deities of mythology are called immortals because they cannot die, unlike humans.

clue.text: Part of film featuring the French soldiers

indicators.note: whatever features something includes it as part of itself, so letters are placed within

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an alien
le is French for the
soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: A section of a movie that stars French troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of film' looks like a single definition, but 'film' belongs to the wordplay and only 'Part' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or constituent of a larger whole.

clue.text: Uniform son wears unadorned voluntarily

definitions.note: adverb clueing a word more often an adjective, though 'came unasked' uses it adverbially

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a wearer has clothing around them, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: naked means bare, without decoration
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy chooses to put on his school uniform plain, without being told.
explanation.walkthrough: The son is wrapped by the bare word, which itself follows the NATO letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without being requested means doing it of your own free will, by choice.

clue.text: Retaliation of noble time and time again on course

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
an era is a period of time
T is the abbreviation for time, used a second time
a tack is a sailing course or line of approach

explanation.surface: An aristocrat keeps getting revenge on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time and time again' looks like an idiom for repeatedly, but each 'time' supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterattack is an attack made in response to one by the enemy, which is retaliation.

clue.text: United regularly hiding section that's unprepossessing

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, out of view

parts.note: something done nightly happens on a regular basis
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A football team keeps concealing an ugly part of the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but here it is a word giving letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprepossessing means unattractive in appearance, and unsightly means ugly to look at.

clue.text: A drug gets one travelling through space?

parts.note: taken as written
a steroid is a drug, often a performance-enhancing one

explanation.surface: A narcotic gets someone so high they are flying through space.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: a space traveller sounds like an astronaut or a tripping drug user.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids are small rocky bodies orbiting the sun, so they literally travel through space.

clue.text: Underwear containing grip popular with good farms

indicators.note: a container holds things within it, so letters go inside

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear
a hold is a grip
something in is fashionable
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Undergarments with elastic grip are popular on decent farms.
explanation.walkthrough: SMALLS is everyday British for underwear; it wraps the other three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a smallholding is a modest agricultural plot, smaller than a typical commercial farm.

clue.text: See German keeping Germany essentially cushy for residents

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so letters go inside

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
GER is the abbreviation for German
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: Look at a German keeping Germany comfortable for its inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'see' and German pieces together close round the Germany letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgers are people who rent a room in someone's house, so they reside there.

clue.text: Supervise six balls with date

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
to see someone is to be dating them

explanation.surface: Look after a juggling act of six balls along with the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six deliveries by one bowler; 'date' is the verb, as in seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct the work of others, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Drink very quietly overlooking old city

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
pp is pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Having a quiet drink with a view over an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old city' looks like the definition, but 'old' is wordplay; in a down answer the first pieces sit over, or overlook, the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria, one of the oldest continuously inhabited places in the world.

clue.text: Superficial journalist settled

parts.note: light reading is superficial, not serious
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A shallow reporter has made up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' is meant in the sense of a bird coming to rest, as in it lighted on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To light on something is to land or come to rest on it, so lighted is a past form meaning alighted.

clue.text: European facing question — competent and calm

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
QU is an abbreviation for question
able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: A European under questioning stays capable and composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competent and calm' looks like a pair of definitions, but only the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An equable person has an even temper and is not easily disturbed, which is to be tranquil.

clue.text: Forbid Juliet's love for music maker

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet
love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Juliet's family ban her romance with a musician, like a Shakespeare plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet suggests Romeo and Juliet, but here she is just the NATO letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument with a round drum-like body, so it is something that makes music.

clue.text: Posh agent spread viruses?

definitions.note: definition by example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: spreading things out scatters them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An upper-class spy is passing on infections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' fits viruses so naturally in the surface that it is easy to miss as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Viruses are one example of pathogens, the germs and microorganisms that cause disease.

clue.text: Brown to leave dance

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown is leaving the party floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina with sharp, dramatic movements.

clue.text: Stone bull seen around New York

indicators.note: a thing found around another encloses it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A bull statue spotted in Manhattan, like the famous Wall Street charging bull.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue picture is a disguise; 'Stone' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious gemstone used for carving.

clue.text: Two promises and an oath

parts.note: first promise: to swear is to vow
second promise: the noun, as in giving your word

explanation.surface: A pair of vows plus a solemn pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oath' looks like a third promise, but it is the curse sense: SWEAR and WORD join to make a rude word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a profane exclamation, a curse, which is what a rude expletive is.
